cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He's just been teaching them how to keep their gatherings orderly (1 Corinthians 14:26-40). Now he says he wants to remind them of the gospel he preached to them.

cards.question: Paul is reminding the Corinthians of the gospel he preached to them. What does he say about how they treat it?

answers.text: They received it and stand firm in it
They argue over every word of it

cards.text: And this isn't just a nice memory, friend. Paul says by this gospel they are saved.

cards.question: Paul puts an "if" on it. The Corinthians are saved by this gospel if they do what?

answers.text: Hold firmly to the word he preached
Keep every feast in the law

cards.question: Paul says that if the Corinthians don't hold firmly to the word he preached, their believing still counts for something.

cards.text: Then Paul gets to what he calls "of first importance". Friend, when Paul says FIRST importance, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: Paul says the message of first importance is something he ___ and then passed on to the Corinthians.

cards.text: First on Paul's list: Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures. Then He was buried.

cards.question: But Paul's list doesn't end with the burial. He says Christ was raised. When?
Paul says Christ being raised happened according to the Scriptures, just like His death.

cards.text: Now Paul brings the receipts: the people the risen Christ appeared to. First, He appears to Cephas, that's Peter (John 1:42).

cards.question: After Cephas, who does Paul say the risen Christ appears to next?

cards.text: Paul's list of people the risen Christ appeared to keeps going, and friend, it gets BIG. Next, He appears to a crowd of brothers, all at once.

cards.question: How many brothers does Paul say see the risen Christ at once?
Paul says most of the brothers who saw the risen Christ all at once have died by the time he writes this letter.

cards.text: Then He appears to someone named James, and then to all the apostles. And Paul's got one more name for the list.

cards.question: Last of all, the risen Christ appears to Paul, the man writing this letter.

cards.text: Paul says it happened to him "as to one of untimely birth." Then he calls himself the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle at all.

cards.question: Why does Paul say he's unworthy to be called an apostle?

answers.text: He persecuted the church of God
He was the youngest of them

cards.text: Paul goes from "the least of the apostles" to "I am what I am" in one breath, friend. That's a BIG turnaround, and something got him there.

cards.question: Paul calls himself the least of the apostles. So what does he say made him what he is now?

cards.text: And Paul says God's grace to him was not in vain. Not one crumb of it wasted, friend.

cards.question: Paul says he worked harder than all of the other apostles.

cards.text: Then Paul adds, "yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me." Friend, I spent years as a worn-out stamper with blurry edges, and when my edges came back SHARP, I sure didn't do it.

cards.question: Whether it was Paul or the others, this is what they ___, and this is what the Corinthians believed.

cards.text: That's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Keep that oven warm, because Paul's not done with this teaching.
